Speaking to Al Jazeera, Haddad pointed to the testing of new air-defence systems in Tehran and other Iranian cities alongside continuing military exercises. He said these preparations indicate that Iranian planners are not basing their security calculations on Trump’s public statements and believe the US president could abruptly change course, including during negotiations. Air defence would be critical in any renewed confrontation involving American or Israeli aircraft, drones or missiles. Haddad also argued that Tehran is preparing for a longer period of pressure from Washington and would treat any diplomatic agreement cautiously rather than assuming the confrontation had ended.
